name: Saint Lucia

income_tax.summary: Income tax is 15% on the first XCD 15,000 of taxable income, 20% on the next XCD 15,000 and 30% above, after a XCD 25,000 personal allowance. Employees pay 5% National Insurance up to XCD 5,000 a month.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: UNVERIFIED, derived: no source for the self-employed National Insurance rate could be found (PwC, Deloitte, Hivedesk and Expanship do not give one; the NIC website could not be reached and the US SSA programme page returns 403). 10% equals the combined employee and employer 5% + 5% (PwC confirms the 5% employee share and that the employer matches it), which is how self-employed contributions are normally set in the OECS schemes, but the real figure and any separate self-employed ceiling remain unconfirmed.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income surtax. Residents with a permanent place of abode are taxed on worldwide income; those resident 183+ days without a permanent abode are taxed on Saint Lucia-source income only. Capital gains are not taxed. A 2.5% health and citizen security levy applies on sales of goods and services (not an income tax). Brackets apply to taxable income after the XCD 25,000 allowance; further deductions (mortgage interest up to XCD 40,000, medical, education) exist.

Saint Lucia: the IRD tax-facts sheet covers 2023-2025 and also caps total allowances and deductions at XCD 30,000; the self-employed 10% rate sits exactly at the 10%-of-assessable-income limit, so it is deductible only if earnings are fully insurable.

rent_2bed_monthly.description: Median asking rent of 4 two-bedroom apartments (Gros Islet USD 1,472 and 2,024, Cap Estate 1,656, Rodney Bay 1,840) among 8 residential rental listings on Terra Caribbean Saint Lucia; furnishing not stated. Very small sample.

source.title: Terra Caribbean: Saint Lucia residential rentals (listing page)

costs.notes: Terra Caribbean Saint Lucia lists only 8 residential rentals (no 1-bedroom unit; the rest are 3 to 5-bedroom houses and a 4-bed townhouse at USD 2,760 to 5,500). Chestertons Saint Lucia returned HTTP 403 and Numbeo HTTP 429.

residence_routes: No remote-worker programme exists in law: the 'Live It' scheme is a tourism marketing label for the standard visitor entry (up to 6 weeks on arrival, extendable in 30-day steps at EC$200) or a multiple-entry non-immigrant visa (EC$190, 12 months) for nationals who need a visa. Skilled employees of a Saint Lucian employer need a work permit (not researched). Citizenship by investment (National Economic Fund, real estate, bonds) is a separate route; amounts not verified. EU, US and other citizens are treated alike in these routes. US citizens remain taxable in the US on worldwide income.
open_questions: No 1-bed rent; the 2-bed figure rests on 4 listings from one agency.
